newsitem.title: UK: Fred.Olsen says considers offshore unit flotation.
newsitem.headline: Fred.Olsen says considers offshore unit flotation.

text.p: Norwegian shipping and oil services group Fred. Olsen Ltd said Tuesday it was considering a public offering for its offshore services unit and would make a decision before the end of the month.
Press reports in Norway said the privately-owned group was planning to issue crowns 2.5 billion crowns' worth of shares in Fred. Olsen Energy Offshore on the Oslo stock exchange.
But Fred Olsen finance director Fridjov Haavardsson said the company had not made a decision to go ahead with an offering.
"I can confirm we have been working on an option to make a public offering," he said, "but no decision has been taken to proceed."
Fred. Olsen Energy currently operates six semi-submersible drilling rigs and supplies offshore services to the oil industry.
Haavardsson said he could not confirm the value of any potential offering or what funds might be used for. But he said: "If we make a public offering it will be a fair size and international."
He added that an announcement would be made before the end of the month.
Haavardsson denied speculation that the Olsen group intends to make its ship owning companies public.
The company has previously said it is reorganising its shipping activities under a new company, Fred. Olsen Shipping, to take advantage of recent changes to the Norwegian tax regime.
Fred.Olsen Energy is currently taking over ownership of the drilling rigs, but new funds are not required for this acquisition, Haavardsson said.
"We can do this without raising money. We have a nice cash flow," he said.
First Olsen Tankers Ltd, the Oslo-listed tanker operator in which the Olsen group retains a 45 percent stake, separately said it did not envisage any of the moves would affect its status.
